title: Market gap mapping for low-latency verticals and fallback economics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Synthesize competitive positioning and unmet needs across enterprise verticals that require sub-50ms to ~150ms inference latency (eg. real-time RAG assistants, voice agents, trading support). Produce a gap map tying vertical buyer pain to achievable throughput/latency profiles and the cost of fallback strategies (quantized models, regional routing, dedicated pools).
problem_statement: Sales and Solutions teams lack a concise, data-backed articulation of which verticals will pay a premium for low-latency inference and how our routing/variant-fallback options materially change TCO and buyer acceptance. We need prioritized verticals, concrete competitive comparisons, and economic thresholds to drive Dedicated and Private conversations.
goals: Identify 6 target vertical pockets (North America + APAC) where sub-100ms median latency materially affects procurement decisions
Estimate per-transaction incremental willingness-to-pay for latency improvements vs. fallback degradations
Produce a decision matrix that maps customer scenarios to recommended Redwood configurations (hosted, dedicated, private) and fallback policies
Deliver one-pager and a granular workbook for Sales/SEs with quick heuristics and links to demos
scope: Include public benchmarks, partner telemetry (where available), customer interview insights, and synthetic workloads. Exclude deep model-architecture optimization work — this is a go-to-market intelligence artifact and an ops playbook for sales enablement.
deliverables: Vertical gap map PDF (one-pager) for Sales deck
Workbook (CSV/Google Sheet) with per-vertical latency buckets, fallback cost delta, and recommended product configuration
Three short demo scripts showing user experience at 40ms vs 200ms for high-priority verticals
Playbook: Sales FAQs and decision heuristics for converting latency-sensitive opportunities
tasks: Run synthetic latency-sensitive microbenchmarks across 4 candidate models (opt, quant, small-flavor) and 3 regions — ENG to provide baseline data (owner: ENG-ops)
Interview 8 field reps and 5 customers across fintech, telehealth, and ecommerce for willingness-to-pay signals (owner: PM research)
Compile competitor public performance claims and pricing for equivalent latency tiers (owner: PM competitive research)
Create cost model comparing hosted token pricing vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs edge/private deployments for typical request volumes (owner: Finance ops)
Draft one-pager and share with Sales and Solutions for review (owner: PM enablement)
Instrument two SLO scenarios in Console demo mode to show fallbacks: model-variant substitution and regional routing (owner: ENG-console)
Finalize workbook and add links to demo artifacts, GitHub PRs, Confluence notes (owner: PM)
Host internal review session and collect signoffs from Sales lead and Product Director (owner: PM)
acceptance_criteria: Workbook contains per-vertical rows with median latency target, estimated buyer WTP, recommended deployment config, and fallback cost delta
One-pager reviewed and approved by Sales lead and Solutions engineering
Benchmarks reproduce in ENG ops lab and are linked from the workbook
At least two demo scripts validated end-to-end by Solutions and shown to one prospective customer in a field call
comments: 2026-03-02 — Liam O'Connor: Kickoff complete; ENG ops confirmed access to regional test clusters. Prioritizing APAC Tokyo and Sydney for edge tests.

2026-03-04 — Jordan Kim (Solutions): From initial interviews, fintech traders tolerate ~30ms tail to maintain UX; telehealth triage tolerates higher median but is sensitive to outliers. Suggested adding 'perceived latency' notes for voice UX demos.

2026-03-05 — Aisha Patel (PM): Decided to prioritize fintech and voice-assist ecommerce as Tier A for sales enablement. Action: ENG-console to prepare two demo SLOs; Finance to model WTP scenarios by 2026-03-12.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: prioritize economical fallbacks (quantized models + prefix caching) vs investing in Dedicated capacity. Need to call out legal/regulatory gating for private deployments in finance verticals. Consider short-run pilot offers (discounted reserved capacity) for anchor customers to validate WTP.
